reasoning_traces.think:
The robust Kelly framework models optimal betting under distributional uncertainty by solving a max-min problem: maximize worst-case expected log utility over an uncertainty set Π of plausible distributions. This formulation ensures long-term growth even when the true distribution is unknown. The key insight is that the worst-case expectation can be computed via convex duality, making it tractable through disciplined convex programming (DCP). In GSE, this translates to a sizing layer where allocation vectors b* are computed by solving the robust optimization problem using uncertainty sets derived from model calibration residuals. The dual nature of the problem allows for efficient computation while maintaining robustness guarantees. However, the method fails if the uncertainty set excludes the true distribution or if the feasible set B lacks convexity. The exogeneity of uncertainty set parameters in the original work necessitates adaptation in GSE to maintain relevance under evolving data conditions.
